draft.title: Patterns, trends and anomalies
card: A pattern is something that repeats or links in results. A trend is the general direction the data moves, such as rising, falling or staying level.
A trend can be described even when the points do not sit exactly on a line. Look at the data as a whole, not at one result.
a result that does not fit the pattern of the others. It stands out as unusually high or low.
An anomaly may come from an error, such as a misread instrument or a spill. Scientists look for the cause and may repeat that trial to check it.
draft.remember: A trend is the overall direction. An anomaly is the result that breaks the pattern.

a.q: Hana times how long ice takes to melt in water at 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 °C. The times fall as the water gets warmer. What does this describe?
opts: A trend: the melting time falls as the temperature rises
An anomaly: the melting time changes between trials
A trend: the melting time rises as the temperature rises
An anomaly: the melting time is the same in every trial
a.why: The times move in one general direction, down as the water warms, so this is a trend. It is not an anomaly, because no single result is out of line with the others.
a.clue: Look at the overall direction of the times.

b.q: Leo measures the height of a bean plant each day for five days: 2 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm, 15 cm, 10 cm. Which statement is best?
opts: 15 cm is an anomaly, so Leo should check how it was measured
The trend is that the plant did not grow at all
15 cm is the trend, because it is the highest result
10 cm is an anomaly, because it is lower than 15 cm
b.why: The heights rise by about 2 cm a day, so 15 cm does not fit and may be a measuring error. Leo should check it. 10 cm is not the anomaly, because it fits the rising trend better.
b.clue: Which result breaks the steady rise?

a.best: A trend: the melting time falls as the temperature rises

b.best: 15 cm is an anomaly, so Leo should check how it was measured
